library_preparation_preflight.summary: spring-batch-infrastructure 6.0.4 declares spring-jdbc (and the other integrations) as optional dependencies, so the JDBC readers and writers, which are a large part of the library, can't be used without them. The flat-file, item-stream, retry and adapter classes only need the compile-scope dependencies spring-core 7.0.8, spring-retry 2.0.13 and spring-context-support 7.0.8. I read the 6.0.4 POM but did not compile or run anything.

deterministic_setup.reason: Optional dependency of spring-batch-infrastructure, pinned to the same Spring Framework version as the library's POM. JdbcCursorItemReader, JdbcPagingItemReader and JdbcBatchItemWriter, and their support classes, need it to load.
In-process database for exercising the JDBC readers and writers without Docker. Version 2.1.210 is already used by the repo's h2 tests.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Use in-memory resources only, with no Docker and no environment variables or system properties. Cover the core readers and writers: FlatFileItemReader and FlatFileItemWriter with DelimitedLineTokenizer, BeanWrapperFieldSetMapper and FieldExtractors, using temp files or ByteArrayResource. Also cover ListItemReader, CompositeItemProcessor and CompositeItemWriter, ItemStream and ExecutionContext handling, and the spring-retry integration. For the JDBC items, use a plain H2 in-memory DataSource (for example DriverManagerDataSource with jdbc:h2:mem:...) and avoid Spring Boot. Skip the optional integrations whose dependencies aren't added (JMS, Kafka, AMQP, Mongo, JPA, Hibernate, XStream and JSON mappers) unless they are added deliberately. Only add a Jackson dependency if the JSON readers and writers are exercised.
risks: The H2 version is an older one chosen to reuse the repo's existing tested version. If the JDBC items misbehave under Spring 7, a newer H2 may be needed, which would be a separate allow-list or version decision.

The reflection-heavy parts (BeanWrapperFieldSetMapper, property access, and any proxies or SpEL in builders) are the likely source of missing-metadata failures. Local Native Image verification is needed to confirm.

Pulling in more of the optional integrations (JPA, JMS, Kafka, Mongo and others) would bring in large dependency graphs and possibly more setup. Keep the scope to spring-jdbc and H2 unless the generated tests need more.
